body.heading: Words that welcome
paragraphs: A welcome sign tells a visitor: we are glad you are here. Write WELCOME in your biggest, friendliest letters.
You could add more languages if your family knows them. Welcome is a word that sounds kind in every language.

body.heading: Decorate it brightly
paragraphs: Fill the spaces with drawings of things that make people happy — flowers, suns, stars, smiling faces.
Bright colours can be read from far away. Your sign should be able to say hello before a visitor even reaches the door.

body.heading: Hang it up
paragraphs: Ask your adult to hang your sign by the front door or on the chair where guests sit.
A small sign does a big job. It turns arriving at your home into a happy moment.

takeaway: A welcome sign is a small thing that does a big job — it makes visitors feel glad they came.
safetyNotes: An adult should hang the sign. Keep paint and water tidy and away from floors where people walk.
screenFreeExtension: Draw mini welcome signs for other places — the cat's bed, the biscuit tin, your own bedroom door.
